inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2025 reported revenue EUR 7,296.1m less ~EUR 162m annualised revenue of the MET Labs (Electrical & Electronic Testing) business (EUR 81.3m in H1 2026, H1-2026 note 2.6), whose sale to UL Solutions closed on 1 October 2026. Its proceeds are carried in equity_bridge instead, so the flows and the bridge do not double-count it. The small loss-making Dutch clinical business sold in January 2026 (~EUR 25m p.a.) is left in the base; immaterial.
inputs.share_count_basis: fully diluted at 30 June 2026: 176,000,000 issued (after the 23 March 2026 cancellation of 6,163,000 treasury shares) less 2,400,532 treasury shares = 173.6m basic, plus 8.2m treasury-stock-method dilution from outstanding options/RSUs (H1-2026 diluted average 183.7m less basic average 175.5m). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so charging dilution as well would double-count. Buybacks (EUR 541m FY2025, EUR 206m H1 2026) fund the flat count.
inputs.debt_composition_note: total_debt = borrowings EUR 4,471.6m at 30 June 2026 less lease liabilities EUR 408.8m (treatment B, leases charged in the flows) = 4,062.8, plus hybrid capital EUR 1,000.0m (IFRS equity, treated as debt-like: fixed coupons 6.75% on the 2028-call tranche, ~EUR 50m/yr paid, ranks ahead of ordinary shares), plus amounts due for business acquisitions EUR 85.7m (44.8 non-current + 40.9 current, deferred consideration). Cash is consolidated cash and equivalents EUR 617.8m excluding the EUR 22.0m held-for-sale cash that transferred with MET Labs. Company-defined net debt (borrowings incl. leases less cash, excl. hybrid) was EUR 3,854m, leverage 2.2x. Post-balance-sheet: the MET Labs proceeds (+EUR 575m, in the bridge) and the Element North American Life Sciences acquisition (~USD 400m / ~EUR 345m, excluded with its revenue under the M&A policy) both settled on 1 October 2026 and roughly offset in net debt.
inputs.interest_income_note: Finance income was EUR 28.3m in FY2025 but Eurofins' operating cash flow starts from profit before tax and adds back 'Finance income and costs, net' (EUR 126.7m), with interest received (EUR 10.7m) shown in investing. Reported OCF/FCF therefore already exclude interest income, and the company is a net debtor (gross cash is netted against borrowings in the bridge), so no further deduction is made.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report, consolidated statement of changes in equity, 'Share-based payment effects' EUR 19.8m (FY2024 21.8m); note 2.6 'Share-based payment charge' -19.8. Equity-award taxes are nil (no net-share settlement; RSUs served from treasury shares). The P&L line 'Share-based payment charge and acquisition-related expenses, net' (EUR 138.1m) is mostly acquisition-related items and is NOT used as SBC.
inputs.last_fcf_note: Owner FCF FY2025 = reported FCF 862.3 (OCF 1,398.9 less gross capex 536.6) less SBC 19.8 less interest income 0 = 842.5, less lease payments 194.0 (repayment of lease liabilities, FY2025 cash flow statement) under lease treatment B = 648.5. The identity reported_fcf - sbc - interest_income holds at 842.5 before the lease line. Company-defined FCFF was EUR 876m (uses net capex of 522.4 after EUR 14.2m disposal proceeds).
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 'Purchase of treasury shares, net of gains' EUR 541.3m (5,466,676 shares at ~EUR 54.7 average, 5.5% of share capital); H1 2026 EUR 205.8m. A repurchaser: the flat count is being paid for.
inputs.price_note: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 54.86-84.92, so the price sits at the top of its range, two days after the 21 October 9M-2026 trading update.
inputs.wacc_rationale: EUR-denominated flows discounted at a EUR-built WACC of 7.5%: 10-year Bund ~3.0% risk-free, 5.5% equity risk premium, levered beta 1.1 (Baa3/BBB- serial acquirer at 2.2x leverage, related-party property dealings) gives a cost of equity ~9.0%; pre-tax cost of debt ~3.8% (bonds 2.75-4%, Schuldschein, hybrid 6.75%) i.e. ~2.8% after 27% tax; market weights ~75% equity (EUR 15.4bn market cap) / 25% debt-like (EUR 5.1bn incl. hybrid). Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality, governance and M&A execution risk are priced in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked onto the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: the full lease payment (principal and interest, FY2025 EUR 194.0m repayment of lease liabilities; H1 2026 EUR 86.0m including ~EUR 9m interest, annualising ~EUR 172m after the FY2025 purchase of 31 leased campuses from the founder family's ABSCA vehicle removed ~EUR 135m of right-of-use assets) is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path, starting at 2.4% of revenue and declining to 2.0% as the 2023-2027 owned-sites programme replaces leases. Lease liabilities (EUR 408.8m) are EXCLUDED from total_debt. da_pct_path is D&A ex right-of-use depreciation: FY2025 total D&A 629.5 (8.6%) less ~EUR 190m ROU depreciation (approximately equal to lease principal on straight-line leases) = ~6.0% of revenue, so the lease is charged once and cash tax is computed on EBIT after the lease charge.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are modelled on the consolidated (total) basis; non-controlling interests are tiny (EUR 31.8m book, EUR 0.3m of H1-2026 profit) and are deducted once as a negative equity_bridge item at book value. Attributable and total net income differ by <1% so no leakage driver is needed.
inputs.hybrid_treatment: EUR 1,000m of perpetual hybrid capital is IFRS equity but carries fixed coupons (6.75% on the EUR 400m 2028-call tranche; EUR 49.7m paid FY2025) and ranks ahead of ordinary shareholders. It is treated as debt-like in total_debt; the coupons are financing flows and are not in EBITDA/owner FCF, so the charge appears exactly once, in the bridge.
inputs.m_and_a_treatment: Eurofins is a serial acquirer (40 deals in FY2025, 17 in H1 2026, EUR 250m p.a. acquired-revenue objective, plus the ~USD 400m Element Materials North American Life Sciences Testing acquisition, >USD 150m revenue, closed 1 October 2026). Acquisition spend and acquired revenue are BOTH excluded from the model: growth paths are organic (FY2026 at the FX-hit pace actually observed), and capex_pct_path covers only organic net operating capex plus the owned-sites programme. Bolt-ons at ~1-1.5x revenue are assumed value-neutral; Element at ~2.3x revenue is roughly neutral at the base 18x FCF cap. Separately disclosed items (restructuring, start-up losses, integration costs; EUR 80m / 1.1% of revenue at EBITDA level in FY2025, objective ~0.5% in FY2027) are treated as recurring for a serial acquirer: ebitda_margin_path is the REPORTED (post-SDI, pre-SBC, IFRS 16) EBITDA margin, not the adjusted figure.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year explicit horizon (FY2026-FY2035) because the margin, lease and capex paths are still normalising through the end of the 2023-2027 investment programme. Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md: operating company, non-US (EUR filer on Euronext Paris), material IFRS 16 leases, hybrid capital, serial acquirer, so owner-fcf.md plus owner-fcf-adaptations.md (a1 currency-matched WACC, b single lease treatment, c NCI once, f risk once) apply. Currency and quote currency are both EUR; no FX bridge. SBC is small (0.27% of revenue) so the house/street band is only ~EUR 2.5 wide and band_position is not a meaningful reading. Base FY2026 revenue growth of 1.5% is the organic, ex-M&A, EUR-reported pace: 9M-2026 revenue grew +3.7% reported including ~1.7pp from acquisitions and a ~-2.5 to -2.9pp USD translation headwind, with organic growth ~3-3.5% and management conceding the full year will land below the original mid-single-digit target. Later years are organic growth between the 3.7-4.7% delivered in FY2024-26 and the 6.5% long-term objective, peaking at 5.0% in the base. Working capital: receivables + contract assets + inventories exceed payables and contract liabilities, so growth consumes cash (wc_capture_pct -5).

equity_bridge.item: MET Labs (Electrical & Electronic Testing) disposal to UL Solutions, EV EUR 575m cash-and-debt-free, signed 14 April 2026 and completed 1 October 2026, net of ~EUR 55m estimated tax and transaction leakage on the ~EUR 370m gain over EUR 205m held-for-sale net assets
equity_bridge.note: H1-2026 interim report note 2.6; the business's revenue (~EUR 162m p.a.) is removed from base_revenue so it is not counted twice. The cash arrived after the 30 June 2026 balance sheet date used for net_debt, which is why it sits in the bridge rather than in cash.
H1-2026 balance sheet; flows are consolidated so the NCI stock is deducted once here.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: management organic-growth objective (6.5% p.a. long-term) tempered by delivered organic growth of 7.1% / 4.7% / 4.1% in FY2023-25 and ~3-3.5% in 9M 2026; every historical CAGR is distorted by the FY2020-22 COVID-testing windfall (FY2021 EBITDA EUR 1,840m vs EUR 1,234m in FY2023) and by EUR 0.9bn of buybacks since 2023 shrinking equity, so none of them is a usable forward anchor
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR (-1.9%) and EPS 3yr CAGR (-8.6%) diverge from revenue (+2.8%) and owner FCF (+23.0%) by far more than 30%: the FY2022 base year still carried COVID-testing earnings, and FY2023-25 buybacks plus hybrid repayment reduced book equity. Owner-FCF and reported-FCF CAGRs are almost identical because SBC is only ~0.3% of revenue and flat.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs computed on reported FCF less SBC (pre-lease adjustment, for a consistent series back to FY2020). Owner FCF: FY2020 851.4, FY2022 453.1, FY2025 842.5 (EUR m).

base.narrative: FY2026 organic growth of 1.5% in EUR (organic ~3.3% less USD translation) per the 9M-2026 walk-back, then reacceleration to a 5.0% peak in FY2028-29 as BioPharma ancillary activities recover, fading to 2.5%. Reported EBITDA margin (post-SDI) 21.4% FY2025 -> 23.0% FY2026 (H1-2026 printed 23.3% reported / 23.7% adjusted) -> 23.5% FY2027, i.e. the 24% adjusted objective less ~0.5% recurring SDI, plateauing at 23.8%. Capex 7.5% in FY2026-27 (EUR 400m net operating + ~EUR 200m owned sites per guidance) stepping down to 6.0% once the programme ends; lease cost 2.4% -> 2.0% as owned sites replace leases. Cash tax 27% (FY2025 ETR 27.7%, FY2024 26.9%).

bull.narrative: The 6.5% organic objective is delivered from FY2028 as biotech funding and ancillary Biopharma activities recover and PFAS/wastewater/FSMA regulation lifts food and environment volumes; adjusted margin passes 25% with SDI at 0.5% once the start-up programme and eLIMS-NG digitalisation complete, so reported margin reaches 24.5%; the owned-sites programme lands on budget and leases fall to 1.8% of revenue; capex normalises to 5.7%.

bear.narrative: Organic growth stays at the ~3% of 2026 (a mature testing network with French clinical reimbursement cuts, Spanish/Italian contract rationalisation, soft biotech funding and USD weakness); SDI remains ~1% of revenue because the group never stops restructuring and integrating 40 bolt-ons a year, so the reported margin stalls at 22.5% despite the 24% adjusted objective; the investment programme runs over and owned-site capex continues past 2027 (capex 8% -> 6.5%); leases are not replaced as fast; tax rate drifts up with Pillar Two.

scenario_narratives.base: Eurofins is the world's largest bio-analytical testing network (~950 laboratories, 59 countries; Life/food-environment 42%, BioPharma 28%, Clinical Diagnostics 21%, Consumer & Technology 10% of ~EUR 7.3bn revenue; Europe 52%, North America 37%), two-thirds of the way through a 2023-2027 programme of buying and building large owned campuses. The base case follows management's FY2026-27 objectives at roughly one year's lag and on a reported (post-SDI) basis: 2026 organic growth of ~3.3% (1.5% in EUR after USD translation) per the 9M-2026 walk-back, recovering to a 5% organic peak rather than the 6.5% objective, the adjusted EBITDA margin reaching 24% with ~0.5% of recurring separately-disclosed items, capex at ~EUR 600m through FY2027 then falling to ~6% of revenue, and lease cost shrinking as owned sites replace rented ones. Acquisitions (including the USD 400m Element North American Life Sciences deal closed 1 October 2026) are excluded from both revenue and spend, so the value is that of the organic business; the EUR 1.0bn hybrid and EUR 86m of deferred consideration are treated as debt. The completed MET Labs disposal (EUR 575m EV) is added through the bridge with its revenue removed from the base.
scenario_narratives.bull: Ancillary BioPharma activities (discovery, genomics, early biotech — the drag since the COVID-testing unwind) recover with the biotech funding cycle and the long-term 6.5% organic objective is met from FY2028, helped by PFAS, EU wastewater and FSMA regulation in food and environment testing and Synlab Spain/Element integration synergies; the margin-accretive owned-sites, hub-and-spoke and eLIMS-NG digitalisation programmes deliver a 25% adjusted margin, SDI falls to 0.5%, and post-2027 capex normalises to ~5.7% of revenue with leases at 1.8%. Cash conversion rises above 50% of EBITDA as guided, buybacks at what management calls an 'historically low valuation' continue, and the market keeps paying ~20x free cash flow for a defensive compounder.
scenario_narratives.bear: Organic growth, which has missed the long-term 6.5% algorithm every year since 2023 and missed FY2026 guidance after the Q1-2026 print (shares -9% on the day), settles at ~3% as food and environment testing mature, French clinical tariff cuts and Spanish/Italian contract rationalisation bite and the dollar stays weak; separately-disclosed items keep recurring at ~1% because the group never stops restructuring and integrating bolt-ons, so the reported margin stalls at 22.5%; the owned-sites programme overruns and keeps capex at 8% of revenue through FY2027 then 6.5%; the governance overhang from the 2024 Muddy Waters report and continuing related-party property transactions with the Martin family's ABSCA vehicle (EUR 298m purchase of 31 campuses in FY2025) caps the multiple at ~14x; leverage at 2.2x plus EUR 1bn of hybrid leaves little room for a misstep on the Element integration.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bear weight up because the thesis carries serial-acquirer and governance risk (related-party ABSCA property dealings behind the 2024 Muddy Waters short report, recurring 'separately disclosed items' that the house basis treats as a real cost, Baa3/BBB- leverage of 2.2x plus EUR 1bn of hybrid ranking ahead of equity, and organic growth that has undershot guidance in 2024, 2025 and 2026). Bull weight down because the bull case needs 6.5% organic growth sustained for five years when the group delivered 3.3-4.7% in FY2024-26, plus a 25% adjusted margin and on-budget completion of the capex programme, several independent things at once. Base keeps 50%: H1-2026 margins (23.7% adjusted) and FCFF (+46%) show the FY2027 profitability objectives are credible even if growth lags.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on the organic business only: SBC expensed and share count held flat, leases charged as an operating cost with lease liabilities excluded from debt, the perpetual hybrid and deferred acquisition consideration treated as debt, separately-disclosed items treated as recurring (reported rather than adjusted EBITDA), M&A spend and acquired growth both excluded, and the completed MET Labs disposal carried in the bridge net of its revenue. Terminal value is the lower of Gordon growth and a free-cash-flow multiple cap (18x base), discounted at a EUR-built 7.5% WACC that is the same in every scenario. Because EUR 4.5bn of debt-like claims sit ahead of equity, per-share value is a levered residual: the hurdle entry price and the required-return table fall much faster with the discount rate than for an unlevered name.
key_risks_to_valuation: Serial-acquirer accounting: if 'separately disclosed items' are genuinely non-recurring the house margin is ~1pp too low (worth roughly EUR 6-7/share); if acquisitions are value-destructive the exclusion of M&A flatters the model, and the USD 400m Element deal at ~2.3x revenue is the first test at scale.

Governance and related-party property: Eurofins leases and buys sites from the founder family's ABSCA vehicle (EUR 298m purchase of 31 campuses in FY2025); the 2024 Muddy Waters report questioned these and the cash balances. A re-rating of trust either way moves the exit multiple more than any driver.
FX: ~37% of revenue is North American and translation is unhedged (-2.2% FY2025, -2.9% H1 2026); the FY2026 base embeds a weaker dollar and a further 10% USD move is ~3-4% of revenue.
Organic growth: the 6.5% objective has not been met since 2021; the base peaks at 5.0% and each 1pp of sustained organic growth is worth ~EUR 5-6/share.
Capex programme: the owned-sites programme (~EUR 200m p.a. through 2027) is assumed to end on schedule; a further year or two at 7.5% capex instead of 6% is worth ~EUR 3-4/share.

Hybrid capital: treating EUR 1,000m of hybrid as debt costs ~EUR 5.5/share versus the IFRS equity presentation; a reader using the company's own net debt (EUR 3,854m incl. leases, excl. hybrid) will get a higher per-share value.

Terminal multiple: the 18x FCF cap binds in every scenario at WACC <= 7.5%, so the sensitivity grid is flat across terminal growth at low discount rates; the market currently pays ~23x company-defined FCFF, so the model assumes a modest de-rating rather than expansion.
Clinical reimbursement and US healthcare enforcement (French tariff cuts since Sept 2024; Boston Heart Diagnostics FCA/AKS history) in the 21% Diagnostics segment.
